title: Integrating Distributed SQL Query Engines with Object-Based Computational Storage
problem: Object storage systems (S3, MinIO) support only basic in-storage filtering, forcing complex operators (aggregation, top-N) to execute at compute layer, causing excessive data movement and query latency.
motivation: Object-based Computational Storage (OCS) enables complex operations within storage, reducing data movement and improving query performance. Integrating OCS with distributed SQL engines requires smart query pushdown analysis to maximize benefit.
method: The Presto-OCS connector analyzes SQL query execution plans to find operations that can run inside the object storage system. Instead of executing expensive operations like aggregations (summing rows into groups), top-N queries (finding the top or bottom values), and joins (combining tables) on a separate compute layer, it pushes these operations into object storage where the data already sits, avoiding massive data transfers across the network. The system was tested on real-world analytics workloads and the TPC-H benchmark.
key_novelty: For the first time, a distributed SQL engine (Presto) can run complex query operations directly in object storage, substantially reducing data movement and improving query speed.
contributions: Presto-OCS connector integrating Presto with Object-based Computational Storage
Query plan analysis for complex operator pushdown eligibility
Support for aggregation, top-N, and join operations in storage
4.07x speedup vs. filter-only pushdown on HPC analytics queries
99% data movement reduction compared to filter-only pushdown
Complementary benefits when combined with compression (1.39x over compressed filter-only)
limitations: OCS device availability and adoption limited. Scalability to very large datasets not evaluated. Applicability to other SQL engines beyond Presto unclear. Cost-benefit analysis vs. network/storage trade-offs not provided.
primary_theme: In-storage query processing for distributed analytics
